description:
Adds a price level. You can use price levels to specify custom pricing for specific customers. Once you create a price level for a customer, QuickBooks will automatically use the custom price in new invoices, sales receipts, sales orders or credit memos for that customer. You can override this automatic feature, however, when you create the invoices, sales receipts, etc.)

The `price_level_add` wrapper from qbXML is also accepted. Returns the v2 request to send, and the webhook payload QuickBooks' answer arrives in (this operation's response_json: its data shape and the status codes to handle).

Possible errors (error.code / error.type; the call result explains each): 1030 unsupported_request, 3000 invalid_object_id, 3040 invalid_amount, 3070 string_too_long, 3100 name_in_use, 3120 object_not_found, 3140 invalid_reference, 3150 missing_element, 3175 in_use, 3176 locked, 3180 cannot_save, 3210 invalid_value, 3220 not_authorized, 3231 request_not_processed, 3250 feature_not_enabled, 3260 insufficient_permission, 3261 personal_data_access_denied, 3262 payroll_subscription_required, 3263 read_only_access, 3264 merchant_services_subscription_required, 3270 missing_posting_account

currency_ref.description:
A currency record defines how QuickBooks stores and displays a currency. Built-in currency name/code values are fixed; formatting and active status can vary by settings and workflow.

Choose exactly one of: `price_level_fixed_percentage`, or the set (`currency_ref`, `price_level_per_item`). Members of a set combine with each other, not with the other choices.

full_name.description: The record's name, parents first: `Jones:Kitchen:Cabinets`. Not case-sensitive.

list_id.description: QuickBooks' ID for the record. Used over `full_name` when both are sent.

include_qbxml.description: Also return the qbXML this compiles to, for debugging. Not part of the v2 request.

is_active.description: If `is_active` is true, this object is currently enabled for use by QuickBooks. The default value is true.

name.description: Name is the case-insensitive short name of a list object (without ancestors). It must be unique within its hierarchy scope.

price_level_fixed_percentage.description:
When you create a price level, you must specify whether it is a fixed percentage or a per item price level. Once you create the price level, you can’t change this.

Choose exactly one of: `price_level_fixed_percentage`, or the set (`currency_ref`, `price_level_per_item`). Members of a set combine with each other, not with the other choices.

price_level_per_item.description: Choose exactly one of: `price_level_fixed_percentage`, or the set (`currency_ref`, `price_level_per_item`). Members of a set combine with each other, not with the other choices.

adjust_percentage.description: Choose exactly one of: the set (`custom_price`, `custom_price_percent`), or the set (`adjust_percentage`, `adjust_relative_to`). Members of a set combine with each other, not with the other choices.

adjust_relative_to.description: Choose exactly one of: the set (`custom_price`, `custom_price_percent`), or the set (`adjust_percentage`, `adjust_relative_to`). Members of a set combine with each other, not with the other choices.

custom_price.description:
When you create a price level, you have the option to create it with a custom price that is either a fixed amount (`custom_price`) or a fixed discount percentage (`custom_price_percent`).

Choose exactly one of: the set (`custom_price`, `custom_price_percent`), or the set (`adjust_percentage`, `adjust_relative_to`). Members of a set combine with each other, not with the other choices.

custom_price_percent.description:
When you create a price level, you have the option to create it with a custom price that is either a fixed amount (`custom_price`) or a fixed discount percentage (`custom_price_percent`).

Choose exactly one of: the set (`custom_price`, `custom_price_percent`), or the set (`adjust_percentage`, `adjust_relative_to`). Members of a set combine with each other, not with the other choices.

item_ref.description: `item_ref` may accept all item types or a restricted subset, depending on the request.

full_name.description: The record's name, parents first: `Jones:Kitchen:Cabinets`. Not case-sensitive.

list_id.description: QuickBooks' ID for the record. Used over `full_name` when both are sent.

request_id.description: Your own label for the request, sent to QuickBooks as its qbXML `requestID` and echoed in the raw answer (`response_xml`); optional, since the answer's webhook already carries the request's `id`.
